jobs.title: Product Manager, Marketplace
jobs.description:
ABOUT HUD

HUD https://www.hud.ai/ is building infrastructure to create RL training data and evals for frontier AI agents, as well as a marketplace to sell these to frontier labs through the HUD marketplace. Our platform is used by frontier labs, Fortune 500 companies, and startups. We’ve raised $16M from top VCs and were YC W25.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking a Product Manager to own product work for our data marketplace. You’ll make it easier for data vendors to bring high-quality RL environments and training data to HUD, and for research teams to discover, evaluate, and use them. You’ll work closely with engineering, research, and GTM to turn technical and operational needs into product decisions.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the marketplace product lifecycle, from understanding vendor and buyer needs through prioritization, launch, and iteration

 - Improve how vendors onboard, submit work, understand quality feedback, and manage their offerings on HUD

 - Improve how research teams discover, assess, and access environments and training data that meet their needs

 - Work with engineering, research, GTM, and operations to turn complex requirements and manual processes into reliable platform workflows

 - Define and track measures of marketplace health, product adoption, and user experience; use feedback and product data to decide what to build next


EXPERIENCE

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Experience owning a live software product from discovery through launch and iteration

 - Strong product judgment and the ability to simplify technically complex workflows for users

 - Experience talking directly with users, identifying the problem behind a request, and turning what you learn into clear priorities

 - Ability to balance user needs, business impact, and engineering constraints when making product decisions

 - Comfort using qualitative feedback and quantitative signals to assess whether a product change worked

 - Clear written communication and the ability to bring engineers and other partners together around decisions in an ambiguous environment

Strong candidates may also have:

 - Experience with marketplaces or products serving two distinct groups of users

 - Familiarity with AI training data, evaluations, and RL environments

 - Experience building a product function or establishing product practices on a growing team

 - Early-stage startup experience and strong communication skills for collaboration across teams and time zones

We prioritize technical aptitude and learning potential over years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet all criteria.


TEAM & COMPANY DETAILS

 - Team Size: ~25 people currently, mostly full-time in-person, but some remote.

 - Our team: Our team includes 4 International Olympiad medalists (IOI, ILO, IPhO), serial AI startup founders, and researchers with publications at ICLR, NeurIPS, etc.

 - Company stage: We have 8 figures in funding and are scaling profitably and quickly to meet very strong demand.


LOGISTICS

 - Employment: Full-time.

 - Location: We have offices in San Francisco or Singapore but are open to remote candidates who can work hours that 70-80% overlap with either San Francisco or Singapore time zones.

 - Visa Sponsorship: We provide support for relocation and visas for strong full-time candidates to the US or Singapore.

 - Timeline: Applications are rolling. The process is 2 technical interviews and a 2-3 day work trial.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - 100% covered top-of-the-line medical, dental, and vision from Blue Shield of CA (US employees)

 - Lunch and dinner when you’re in the office (in-office employees)

 - Company-wide holiday break (Christmas Eve to New Year’s Day) on top of PTO and paid holidays

 - Other perks including an Equinox membership, 401k, and commuter benefits (US employees)

 - Unlimited* access to tokens for ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, etc. *By unlimited, we mean no one on our token usage leaderboard has ever hit a limit. So we have no idea what the limit is.

Due to high volume, we may not actively respond to every application, but feel free to contact us at recruiting@hud.so or elsewhere if we missed your application!

jobs.title: Manufacturing Data & Process AI Integration System Engineer, Additive Manufacturing
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



What You'll Do

 - Monitoring and Analytics Layer: Own the monitoring and analytics layer for the AM fleet — what is computed from raw machine and build data, what is surfaced, and what triggers an alert, at the fidelity traceability and modeling require.

 - Analytical Data Layer: Own the curated datasets, feature definitions, labeling, and dataset versioning, built on the canonical machine data model and pipelines owned by the Machine Controls & Data Integration Engineer.

 - AI/ML Model Development: Design, develop, and deploy models trained on Hadrian manufacturing data to predict build quality, detect process anomalies, and identify parameter optimization opportunities.

 - Model Infrastructure: Build and maintain the feature engineering and model infrastructure — data quality checks, labeling workflows, model versioning, and model performance tracking in production.

 - Dashboards and Alerting: Develop process monitoring dashboards and AI-driven alerting that give engineering and operations real-time visibility into machine and build health.

 - Closing the Loop: Integrate model outputs back into OPUS and the manufacturing workflow so predictions drive action, and work toward closed-loop parameter adjustment.

 - Physical Validation with M&P: Collaborate with Materials and Process and Application Engineering to validate model outputs against physical process knowledge before they influence production decisions.

 - Statistical Process Control: Apply SPC to AM process data, and establish the control limits and drift detection that flag a machine leaving its qualified operating envelope.

 - Qualification Analysis Support: Supply capability, repeatability, and process analysis in support of qualification — machine capability data to the System Qualification Engineer for installation and operational qualification, and performance qualification analysis support to Materials and Process and Application Engineering for customer data packages.

 - Data-Driven Problem Solving: Lead structured problem-solving on process escapes and build anomalies using 8D, 5 Whys, and fishbone analysis, driving corrective and preventive action to verified closure.
   

What we're Looking For

 - Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Materials Science, or related field.

 - 4+ years in manufacturing data systems, process engineering, or data-driven manufacturing in a production environment.

 - Hands-on experience developing and deploying AI/ML models in an engineering or manufacturing context, including model training, validation, and production deployment.

 - Proficiency in Python and relevant ML frameworks (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, or equivalent), and SQL fluency for working with manufacturing data at scale.

 - Experience building analytical datasets from structured and time-series manufacturing data, including handling of gaps, resampling, and data quality problems.

 - Familiarity with structured problem-solving methodologies (8D, 5 Whys, fishbone) and statistical process control.

 - Strong analytical skills, with the ability to connect model outputs to physical process understanding and actionable engineering decisions.

 - Ability to work on site full time in Torrance, California, with travel up to 15% [CONFIRM].

 - Must be a U.S. person for ITAR purposes — a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or otherwise eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
   

What Will Set You Apart

 - Experience applying AI/ML to metal additive manufacturing — build quality prediction, anomaly detection, melt pool monitoring, or process parameter optimization.

 - Background with in-situ process monitoring data: layer imaging, thermal sensing, acoustic emissions, or scanner and galvanometer telemetry.

 - Experience supporting qualification data packages for aerospace, defense, or regulated manufacturing environments.

 - Familiarity with AMS7032, NIAR/NCAMP, or US Navy AM qualification requirements.

 - Experience with MLOps practices — model versioning, monitoring, retraining pipelines, and production deployment.

 - Experience with closed-loop or feedback control of a manufacturing process using model output.


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

jobs.title: Apprentice Technician
jobs.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

• Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

• What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

• It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

YOUR MISSION

As an Apprentice Technician, you will support spacecraft production, mechanical assembly, integration, and testing while developing the skills needed to become a well- rounded spacecraft technician. This entry-level role is designed for individuals with limited
industry experience who are eager to learn through hands-on training, mentorship, and cross-functional exposure.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Mechanical Assembly and Integration: Support the assembly and integration of spacecraft structures, components, mechanisms, panels, brackets, fasteners, and flight
hardware. Assist with the installation and removal of components under the guidance of experienced technicians.
Basic Mechanical Operations: Perform fastening, torquing, taping, hardware installation, part preparation, and other basic mechanical tasks after appropriate training.
Test Support: Assist with spacecraft and component test setup and execution, including functional and environmental testing, fixture installation, test equipment setup, and post- test activities.Tools and Documentation: Learn to safely use hand tools, power tools, torque tools, measuring equipment, and production equipment. Read and follow drawings, work instructions, procedures, and manufacturing documentation.
Shop and Material Support: Support hardware movement, material handling, tool control, shop organization, inventory activities, and general production needs.
Safety and Quality: Follow FOD, ESD, cleanliness, hardware-handling, personal protective equipment, and shop safety requirements. Document completed work and communicate discrepancies or concerns to technicians, leads, engineers, and management.
Cross-Training: Develop skills across mechanical production, spacecraft integration, and test. Flex between work areas as production priorities and program needs change.

QUALIFICATIONS

• High school diploma or equivalent.
• 0–1 year of manufacturing, mechanical, technical, automotive, aerospace, aviation,
electronics, or similar hands-on experience.
• Basic mechanical aptitude and willingness to learn.
• Comfort working with hand tools, power tools, and measuring equipment.
• Ability to follow detailed written and verbal instructions.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to safety and quality.
• Reliable, team-oriented, and willing to take on new responsibilities.
• Ability to work across multiple areas of a production shop.
• Ability to lift 25 pounds and work in and around constrained or confined spaces.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Trade school, technical school, apprenticeship, or relevant technical training.
• Experience or coursework in manufacturing, mechanical systems, automotive,
aviation, aerospace, electronics, machining, or a related field.
• Exposure to engineering drawings, work instructions, torque tools, calipers, gauges, or other measurement equipment.
• Previous experience in manufacturing, production, maintenance, laboratory, or technical environment.

COMPENSATION

• Base Salary: Apprentice Technician: $24-33/hr *this position is non-exempt and is eligible for overtime

• Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Work Location—this a fully onsite position based out of our Long Beach, CA office.

• Work environment—the work environment; temperature, noise level, inside or outside, or other factors that will affect the person's working conditions while performing the job.

• Physical demands—the physical demands of the job, including bending, sitting, lifting and driving.

This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below. #LI-Onsite

jobs.title: Mechanical Spacecraft Technician (I–III)
jobs.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

• Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

• What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

• It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

YOUR MISSION

As a Mechanical Spacecraft Technician, you will play a vital role in the assembly, integration, and testing of spacecraft mechanical systems. You will collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to build spacecraft hardware from early development through environmental testing, flight readiness, and production ramp. This role may be leveled from Technician I to Technician III based on experience, skills, and demonstrated proficiency.

RESPONSIBILITIES
Mechanical Assembly: Build, install, and inspect spacecraft mechanical hardware—including primary and secondary structures, panels, brackets, payloads, mechanisms, deployables, thermal hardware, fasteners, and support equipment—using engineering
drawings, work instructions, and process documentation.
Component Preparation and Handling: Prepare, clean, protect, and handle flight and flight-like hardware. Perform precision assembly operations including torqueing, safety wiring, staking, bonding, shimming, alignment, and mechanical fastening while maintaining hardware traceability and configuration control.
Spacecraft Integration: Support the integration of mechanical subsystems and components into spacecraft structures. Install and route hardware, perform fit checks and dimensional inspections, and support closeouts and access panel installation.
Testing and Validation: Support mechanical functional testing, deployment testing, alignment checks, mass properties measurements, vibration testing, acoustic testing, thermal vacuum testing, and other environmental test activities. Set up test hardware and
fixtures, follow approved procedures, and accurately record results.
Inspection and Troubleshooting: Perform visual, dimensional, and workmanship inspections. Identify and document hardware discrepancies, support nonconformance investigations, and work with engineering and quality teams to resolve assembly and integration issues.
Tooling and Ground Support Equipment: Operate and maintain hand tools, torque tools, precision measurement equipment, lifting equipment, assembly fixtures, and mechanical ground-support equipment. Support the development and improvement of tooling and work instructions.
Safety and Compliance: Follow requirements for FOD prevention, ESD control, cleanroom operations, hazardous materials, lifting and handling, contamination control, and safe work around energized and flight hardware.
Continuous Improvement: Provide feedback on assembly processes, drawings, work instructions, tooling, and manufacturing methods to improve safety, quality, repeatability, and schedule performance.

QUALIFICATIONS
• Technical degree, certificate, apprenticeship, or equivalent training in mechanical, aerospace, manufacturing, or a related field.
• Relevant experience in spacecraft, aerospace, defense, automotive, precision manufacturing, or other high-reliability mechanical assembly environments.
• Experience assembling and integrating mechanical structures, mechanisms, brackets, panels, fasteners, or related hardware.
• Proficiency reading engineering drawings, schematics, work instructions, process sheets, and assembly procedures.
• Experience using hand tools, torque tools, precision measurement equipment, and mechanical test equipment.
• Experience with mechanical alignment, dimensional inspection, shimming, bonding, staking, or safety wiring.
• Experience working in ESD-sensitive, FOD-critical, and cleanroom environments.
• Ability to follow detailed procedures and maintain accurate build, inspection, and
test documentation.
• Ability to work autonomously and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to lift 25 pounds and work in and around constrained or confined spaces.

LEVELING GUIDANCE
Technician I: Develops proficiency in spacecraft mechanical assembly, hardware handling, documentation, and inspection while working under regular guidance. Typically has 0–1 years of relevant experience or equivalent technical training.
Technician II: Independently performs a broad range of mechanical assembly, integration, inspection, and test activities. Troubleshoots common issues and supports process improvements and peer training. Typically has 1–3 years of relevant experience.
Technician III: Performs complex mechanical assembly, integration, troubleshooting, and testing with limited supervision. Serves as a technical resource for other technicians and supports development hardware, environmental testing, flight readiness, and production ramp. Typically has 3+ years of relevant experience or equivalent demonstrated proficiency.

PREFERRED SKILLS
• Spacecraft or satellite mechanical assembly and integration
• Experience with primary and secondary spacecraft structures
• Mechanical mechanisms, deployment systems, hinges, latches, or release devices
• Precision alignment and dimensional inspection
• Torque application, safety wiring, staking, shimming, and mechanical fastening
• Structural bonding, potting, or adhesive application
• Experience supporting vibration, acoustic, thermal vacuum, or other environmental testing
• Experience with lifting and handling flight hardware
• Familiarity with GD&T and mechanical inspection practices
• Experience with composite structures, lightweight materials, or additive-manufactured hardware
• Experience using coordinate measuring machines, laser trackers, optical tooling, or other alignment equipment
• Relevant certifications in mechanical assembly, rigging, machining, composites, or cleanroom operations

COMPENSATION

• Base Salary: Technician I : $26.50-$36/hr Technician II: $31.50-$41.50/hr Technician III: $36-50.50/hr *this position is non-exempt and is eligible for overtime

• Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Work Location—this a fully onsite position based out of our Centennial, CO office.

• Work environment—the work environment; temperature, noise level, inside or outside, or other factors that will affect the person's working conditions while performing the job.

jobs.title: Senior Director, GTM Revenue Operations
jobs.description:
About Us:
 
ChowNow is one of the leading players in off-premise restaurant technology. As takeout becomes a vital revenue stream for independent restaurants, our platform helps owners focus on what they do best—serving great food—by offering solutions across the entire digital dining experience. From building branded websites and mobile apps, to powering online orders, managing menus, consolidating delivery, and running targeted marketing, we give restaurants the tools to grow on their own terms.
 
We support thousands of restaurants across North America, helping process $1B+ in gross food sales while saving our partners over $700M in third-party commission fees. Through our white-label ordering solutions, a growing demand network (including Google, Yelp, Apple, and Snap), and a diner-friendly marketplace, we empower independent restaurants to own their customer relationships and avoid inflated pricing and fees charged by 3rd party delivery apps like Uber and Doordash. 
 
Founded in 2012, we’ve navigated rapid growth and transformation—from startup roots through the pandemic boom—and are now beginning an exciting new era under our CEO, Kanika Soni. As we evolve with new leadership and cutting-edge tools, we’re deepening our commitment to helping local restaurants thrive in the digital economy.
 
About the Position:
The Senior Director, GTM Revenue Operations, is both the strategic and technical backbone of how ChowNow's Sales, Onboarding, and Customer Success teams operate day to day. This is not a reporting-and-dashboards role — it's an operator and systems-architect role. You'll need to understand the GTM motion deeply enough to sit in a rep's or post sales rep’'s shoes, spot exactly where a process is broken or a workflow is creating friction, and then personally architect the fix — not as an isolated patch, but as part of a coherent system that holds up as we scale.
This function exists because of where the business is today: years of incremental, band-aid fixes and one-off customizations have left us with real tech debt across Salesforce, HubSpot, PlanHat, and the tools connecting them. Small changes take too long, and they too often break something else in the process. We need someone who can see the whole board — not just the piece in front of them — untangle what's been glued together, and rebuild it so that future changes are fast, safe, and durable.
You'll lead three key functions: a Sales & CS Business Ops (who lives inside the sales and CS org, diagnosing friction and defining the fix), a Marketing & Partner Ops Manager (who owns the demand and partner tech stack end to end as our HubSpot admin), and a Biz Systems team who build and maintain our core systems. Your job is to make sure these three functions work as one connected system rather than three disconnected ones — translating GTM needs into technical requirements, and technical constraints back into GTM strategy, so nothing gets lost in either direction.
This role reports directly to the CEO and will own a team of 5-7 direct reports.
This is a remote role based in the United States. Please note: ChowNow is not eligible to employ in every state and the recruiting team will confirm location and eligibility before moving past initial stages.
 
WHAT WE LOVE ABOUT YOU:
 
You put restaurants first. You deeply understand the importance of local restaurants and put them at the center of everything you do. You aim to help them not only survive but thrive.
 
You celebrate diversity. You recognize that diversity and inclusivity matter. You’re committed to progress, which means everyone gets the support and resources they need, no matter who they are.  You have an ability to listen to other team members' ideas and can thrive in an environment that embraces individuality. Everyone’s voice counts.
 
You raise your hand. You consistently go above and beyond what is asked of you. You help your peers accomplish their tasks while also excelling at accomplishing your own. When you have a smart idea, you raise your hand and share it.
 
You keep reaching. You set clear ambitious goals. You don’t allow yourself to become complacent with where you’re at and what you’ve done, so you seek out new opportunities and challenges.

jobs.title: Sr. IT Systems Engineer, DevOps
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. IT SYSTEMS ENGINEER, DEVOPS

SpaceX is looking for a Senior IT Systems Engineer with a focus on DevOps to join our growing team. You will own the architecture, design, implementation, and evolution of our CI/CD platforms, infrastructure automation, and reliability engineering practices at scale, including on-premise VM and Kubernetes infrastructure. This employee will be a senior member of the Information Technology IT Applications team. The ideal candidate will be a technical leader who is flexible and flourishes in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment. He or she should be a self-starter, self-motivator, and possess the ingenuity and ownership to excel at this position while mentoring others.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Architect, design, implement, and manage enterprise-scale CI/CD pipelines and platforms running on both on-premise VM infrastructure and Kubernetes clusters.

• Lead automation of deployment, configuration, monitoring, and operations to drive reliability, scalability, and efficiency across hundreds of on-premise servers, VMs, and containerized environments.

• Define and enforce DevOps, SRE, and release engineering best practices, standards, and security controls across on-premise VM and Kubernetes infrastructure.

• Partner closely with software engineering, development, and operations teams to streamline code integration, testing, delivery, and feedback loops.

jobs.title: Machine Controls & Data Integration System Engineer, Additive Manufacturing
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



What You'll Do

 - Machine Connectivity Across the Fleet: Build and own the connectivity layer across the AM fleet — PC-based machine control systems, PLC-based subsystems, and vendor interfaces alike — including the log, file, and tag-level extraction required where no standard interface exists.

 - Canonical Data Model and Schema Governance: Own the schemas, tag dictionaries, naming conventions, units, and versioning that let one integration pattern scale across platforms and sites. Govern schema change so downstream consumers do not break.

 - Pipelines and Storage: Design, build, and operate the telemetry and build data pipelines — transport, stream processing, buffering, and persistence into relational and time-series storage — with the uptime, backfill, and data integrity guarantees that qualification evidence depends on.

 - Machine State Models and OPUS Integration: Own how a machine reports what it is doing, how work is dispatched to it, and how each build record ties to part, powder lot, machine, and operator for end-to-end traceability.

 - Requirements and Interface Baseline: Define the interface, control, and data requirements; flow them down to OEMs and to internal engineering; verify what is delivered against them; and hold the change-controlled interface control documents — state models, command semantics, telemetry dictionaries, alarm and error handling, and version history — so every integration is specified before it is built, reproducible across machines and sites, and enforceable with vendors as their platforms and firmware evolve.

 - Supplementary Instrumentation: Instrument what the OEM does not expose. Specify and integrate supplementary sensing, edge compute, and data acquisition where native machine data is insufficient for process monitoring or engineering investigation.

 - OT Network and Controller Accreditation: Partner with IT and Security to get machine controllers onto a compliant network — segmentation, remote access, patch and firmware change paths, and controller accreditation under NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC.

 - Safety State Integration: Integrate machine and cell safety state into the control and platform layer, and validate interlock behavior against aerospace and defense production requirements, in coordination with the Automation & Robotics Engineer and site EHS.

 - Commissioning and Acceptance Support: Support commissioning, Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) from a controls and connectivity standpoint, ensuring each machine meets the Hadrian integration standard before production release.

 - Build Preparation Toolchain Handoff: Support the build preparation and slicing toolchain integration path — the handoff from build preparation software into machine execution and back into the manufacturing record — in partnership with Application Engineering and the software team.

 - OEM Technical Relationships: Establish and maintain OEM relationships covering interface and data access, controller and firmware change management, calibration hooks, and serviceability — including holding vendors to the agreed interface requirements through platform and firmware changes.

 - Qualification Data Foundation: Supply the data integrity, audit trail, and configuration control support the System Qualification Engineer needs for installation and operational qualification, and that Materials and Process and Application Engineering need for performance qualification.

 - Structured Problem Solving: Lead structured problem-solving on integration, connectivity, and data anomalies using 8D, 5 Whys, and corrective action driven to verified closure.
   

What we're Looking For

 - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, Mechatronics, or related field.

 - 5+ years connecting production manufacturing equipment to higher-level software systems — MES, SCADA, historian, or equipment and data platforms — with direct hands-on ownership of the integration rather than oversight of an integrator.

 - Hands-on fluency with industrial machine communication: OPC-UA and MQTT, plus at least one PLC platform at the tag and program level. Siemens S7 and TIA Portal strongly preferred; PROFINET, EtherNet/IP, or Modbus equivalents considered. Working familiarity with MTConnect and REST APIs.

 - Demonstrated ability to integrate proprietary or undocumented OEM interfaces — working out log formats, file drops, and vendor data access where no standard protocol is available.

 - Strong database engineering: relational schema design and SQL fluency, plus practical experience with time-series or historian storage for high-rate machine data. Schema migration and versioning experience required.

 - Experience designing and operating data pipelines in production — message transport, stream or batch processing, and monitoring of the pipeline itself.

 - Working proficiency in Python or equivalent for integration, parsing, and data tooling, with version control and code review discipline.

 - Experience implementing or validating safety interlock systems in a production manufacturing environment.

 - Demonstrated ability to define technical interface and data requirements, flow them down to equipment vendors and internal engineering teams, verify delivered systems against them, and keep change-controlled interface documentation current as those systems evolve.

 - Ability to work on site full time in Torrance, California, and to travel to Hadrian deployment sites and OEM facilities — up to 25% [CONFIRM].

 - Must be a U.S. person for ITAR purposes — a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or otherwise eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
   

What Will Set You Apart

 - Experience with metal additive manufacturing equipment — LPBF controller architecture, laser and scanner control, or in-process monitoring.

 - Experience integrating equipment into MES or factory data platforms in aerospace or defense production.

 - Experience with AM process data: in-situ monitoring, melt pool sensing, layer imaging, or scanner and galvanometer telemetry.

 - Experience with OT network architecture and security in a regulated or defense manufacturing environment, including NIST SP 800-171 or CMMC.

 - Exposure to polymer AM platforms alongside metal.

 - Familiarity with aerospace and defense AM qualification data requirements — AMS7032, US Navy, or NIAR/NCAMP.

 - Experience supporting installation and operational qualification from a controls and data integrity perspective.




BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

jobs.description:

Join a team of brilliant, passionate innovators determined to transform healthcare. At BillionToOne, we've built a category-defining, publicly traded company on Nasdaq where transparency fuels trust, collaboration drives breakthroughs, and every contribution moves the needle on our mission to make life-changing diagnostics accessible to all. We don't just aim for incremental improvements; we build products that are 10x better than anything that exists today.

Our scientists, engineers, sales executives, and visionaries are united by an unwavering commitment to changing the standard of care in prenatal and cancer diagnostics. This is where cutting-edge science meets human compassion, and every innovation you contribute helps remove the fear of the unknown from some of life's most critical medical moments.

If you're driven by purpose, energized by innovation, and ready to help shape the future of precision medicine at scale, this is where you belong.

We are looking for a Phlebotomy Operations Specialist to manage and grow BillionToOne’s national phlebotomy network in support of our Unity prenatal (NIPT) testing. This role sits at the intersection of operations, scheduling, and vendor support — you’ll be the connective tissue between our Sales Operations (SOPS) team, our phlebotomy network, and the patients we serve.

The Phlebotomy Operations Specialist holds a pivotal role in the organization, managing and growing our network of In-Office Phlebotomists (IOP) and Patient Service Center (PSC) phlebotomists across the country. The ideal candidate for this role is an ambitious and highly organized individual who is comfortable owning logistics at a national scale and who works well cross-functionally with sales, contracts, and operations teams.

The Phlebotomy Operations Specialist is a full-time remote position and reports to the Phlebotomy and Vendor Operations Manager.

Working hours are Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM local time, based on business needs.

Responsibilities:

• Recruit, place, and manage In-Office Phlebotomists (IOP) on a national scale.

• Recruit, place, and manage PSC-based phlebotomists across our growing site network.

• Support the setup of new Patient Service Centers (PSC), including site identification, staffing, and readiness for launch.

• Build and maintain relationships with phlebotomy vendors and site partners nationwide.

• Own the scheduling process for both IOP and PSC phlebotomists, ensuring consistent coverage and minimal service gaps.

• Manage end-to-end onboarding for new phlebotomists, including credentialing, training coordination, and compliance documentation.

• Manage phlebotomy supply inventory across sites (draw kits, PPE, shipping supplies, etc.).

• Monitor stock levels and coordinate replenishment to prevent disruptions to draw operations.

• Serve as the operational point of contact for the Sales team on all phlebotomy-related needs for the NIPT product line.

• Ensure timely, accurate responses to sales inquiries regarding phlebotomy coverage and site status.

• Deliver best-in-class support that reflects BillionToOne's patient-first mission.

Qualifications:

• Experience in phlebotomy operations, healthcare staffing, or vendor management (healthcare/diagnostics industry preferred).

• Proven ability to manage multiple priorities across a distributed, national network.

• Strong organizational skills with comfort owning scheduling and logistics at scale.

• Clear, proactive communicator who works well cross-functionally with sales, contracts, and operations teams.

• Comfortable working with data and operational metrics to track network performance.

• 4-year college degree or equivalent experience required.

jobs.title: Assistant Director of Rooms

The Assistant Director of Rooms supports the overall leadership, strategic direction, and operational effectiveness of the Rooms Division. The position must be able to identify performance gaps, address challenging issues directly and constructively, and translate observations and data into sustainable corrective actions.

The Assistant Director of Rooms acts as a senior operational leader who anticipates challenges, resolves complex issues, and strengthens communication and collaboration among Front Office, Fairmont Gold, Housekeeping, Royal Service, and other supporting departments. The position serves as a visible and credible leader for guests and colleagues and may assume leadership responsibility for the Rooms Division in the absence of the Hotel Manager.

• Serve as a key leadership resource and partner to the Director of Front Office and Director of Housekeeping, providing guidance, support, and assistance with operational priorities and complex issues.

• Support the Directors of Front Office and Housekeeping in achieving departmental goals, operational standards, guest satisfaction objectives, and financial targets.
• Promote effective communication and collaboration between Front Office, Housekeeping, Fairmont Gold, Royal Service, and other hotel departments.
• Ensure consistent adherence to Fairmont Hotels & Resorts standards, service expectations, policies, procedures, and brand initiatives.
• Promote a culture of service excellence, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Financial & Business Performance

• Support the Rooms Division leadership team in achieving departmental financial and operational objectives.
• Assist with the preparation, monitoring, and analysis of Rooms Division budgets, forecasts, and financial results.
• Review operational and financial performance indicators and identify opportunities to improve productivity, efficiency, and profitability.
• Support effective labor management and staffing strategies while maintaining appropriate service levels.
• Assist with monitoring Rooms Division revenue and expense performance and provide recommendations to leadership as appropriate.
• Support initiatives designed to maximize room revenue, occupancy, guest satisfaction, and overall hotel profitability.
• Participate in the development and execution of annual strategic plans and departmental initiatives.

Guest Experience & Service Excellence

• Champion a consistently exceptional, personalized, and emotionally engaging guest experience across all Rooms Division areas.

• Review guest feedback, service recovery trends, quality assurance findings, and operational data daily to identify patterns, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
• Ensure thorough and objective follow-up on guest concerns by reviewing all relevant information and perspectives, including the guest experience, colleague actions, operating processes, communication, and leadership oversight.
• Support the development and implementation of service enhancements that anticipate guest needs, strengthen personalization, and exceed luxury hospitality expectations.
• Handle highly escalated guest concerns with empathy, professionalism, discretion, emotional intelligence, and appropriate urgency.
• Partner with department leaders to identify recurring service issues and implement sustainable solutions with defined ownership, timelines, and measurable outcomes.
• Track the effectiveness of corrective actions and adjust the approach when guest satisfaction, quality assurance, or operational results do not demonstrate sufficient improvement.
• Recognize and celebrate colleague contributions, service excellence, and meaningful improvements that positively affect the guest experience.
• Reinforce that genuine luxury service requires both warmth and disciplined execution, including accuracy, timeliness, anticipation, ownership, personalization, and consistent follow-through.

Colleague Leadership & Development

• Support the Directors of Front Office and Housekeeping in the recruitment, onboarding, training, development, and retention of Rooms Division colleagues.
• Promote a culture of engagement, inclusion, accountability, and professional development.
• Help department leaders strengthen their own ability to coach, communicate, delegate, make decisions, resolve conflict, and hold their teams accountable.
• Create a supportive environment in which colleagues feel valued, respected, and empowered while maintaining clear expectations for performance, behavior, reliability, and results.
• Demonstrate personal accountability by seeking feedback, acknowledging mistakes, adjusting approaches when necessary, and remaining committed to continuous leadership development.

Salaried Position with Range of 119,364K - 122,364K Annually

Education & Experience

• Bachelor’s degree in Hospitality Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline preferred.
• Minimum of 3 - 5 years of demonstrated leadership experience within Front Office, Housekeeping or Rooms Division.
• Previous management experience within a full-service, luxury, or upscale hotel environment required.
• Comprehensive knowledge of Rooms Division operations, including Front Office, Housekeeping, guest services, service recovery, room inventory management, and interdepartmental coordination.
• Demonstrated success in supporting and partnering with department leaders to improve operational execution, financial performance, colleague engagement, and guest satisfaction.
• Proven ability to establish credibility and work in close alignment with the Hotel Manager, department leaders, and other members of the hotel’s leadership team.
• Experience with scheduling, labor management, productivity measurement, expense control, and financial control required.

• Advanced ability to resolve escalated guest concerns, sensitive colleague matters, and complex operational situations with professionalism, discretion, fairness, and sound judgment.
• Demonstrated ability to co connect, coach, train, develop colleague and improve team performance.
• Proven ability to address performance gaps constructively, establish clear expectations, and achieve measurable improvement through coaching, accountability, and consistent follow-through.
• Demonstrated leadership maturity, emotional intelligence, resilience, adaptability, and the ability to remain objective when navigating challenging interpersonal or operational circumstances.
• Ability to consider multiple perspectives, receive feedback openly, challenge assumptions appropriately, and adapt decisions when new information becomes available.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and the ability to effectively utilize applicable hotel systems and technology, including property management, guest service, housekeeping, scheduling, quality assurance, reporting, and other operational systems.
• Ability to learn, adopt, and effectively utilize new computer programs, hotel systems, and technology as required.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to occasionally bend, stoop, reach, climb stairs, and navigate hotel work areas.

Mental Requirements

Other Abilities, Skills, and Knowledge

jobs.title: Sr. Staff / Principal Physical Design Engineer
jobs.description:
About the Company:

At SK hynix memory solutions, we're at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, developing advanced memory solutions that power everything from smartphones to data centers. As a global leader in NAND flash technology and memory solutions, we drive the evolution of advancing mobile technology, empowering cloud computing, and pioneering future technologies. Our cutting-edge memory technologies are essential in today's most advanced electronic devices and IT infrastructure, enabling enhanced performance and user experiences across the digital landscape.

We're looking for innovative minds to join our mission of shaping the future of technology. At SK hynix memory solutions, you will be part of a team that's pioneering breakthrough memory solutions while maintaining a strong commitment to sustainability. We're not just adapting to technological change – we're driving it, with significant investments in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and eco-friendly solutions and operational practices. As we continue to expand our market presence and push the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor technology, we invite you to be part of our journey to creating the next generation of memory solutions that will define the future of computing.

About the Role

Join our Physical Design(SoC Integration)  team responsible for delivering high-performance SoC designs from RTL to GDS. As a Sr. Staff Physical Design Engineer, you will lead physical implementation efforts for advanced-node designs, driving critical blocks through synthesis, placement, CTS, routing, and signoff. You will work closely with front-end, DFT, power, and analog teams to optimize PPA (Power, Performance, Area) while ensuring silicon success. This role requires deep hands-on expertise across the full physical design flow as well as leadership to mentor junior engineers and define methodologies for the team.

Responsibilities

• Lead physical design implementation from synthesis through GDS for high-performance blocks or full-chip SoC designs in advanced process nodes (7nm, 5nm, 3nm)

• Execute and optimize synthesis, placement, clock tree synthesis (CTS), and routing using industry-standard P&R tools (Synopsys ICC2/Fusion Compiler or Cadence Innovus)

• Drive timing closure and signoff using PrimeTime (PT), including advanced analysis such as SI, AOCV/POCV, crosstalk, and ECO implementation

• Perform RC extraction using StarRC or Quantus and ensure strong correlation between extraction and STA results

• Own physical verification signoff with Mentor/Siemens Calibre, resolving DRC, LVS, ERC, and antenna violations in complex FinFET layouts

• Conduct power integrity analysis using Ansys RedHawk(Redhawk-SC), including static/dynamic IR drop and EM analysis; implement power grid and decap optimizations

• Develop and maintain physical design flows and automation scripts (Tcl, Perl, Python), mentor junior engineers, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to achieve tapeout schedules

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field (Master's preferred)

• 8+ years of hands-on experience in ASIC physical design with proven tapeout success

• Expert-level proficiency in synthesis, placement, CTS, and routing using Synopsys or Cadence P&R tools

• Deep knowledge of static timing analysis (STA) and PrimeTime signoff, including multi-corner/multi-mode closure

• Demonstrated experience with physical verification using Calibre (DRC, LVS, ERC) and IR drop/EM analysis using RedHawk

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience at 5nm or 3nm process nodes with FinFET and multi-patterning design rules

• Familiarity with low-power design techniques including UPF, clock gating, multi-Vt, and voltage islands

• Strong programming skills in Tcl, Perl, and Python for flow automation and data analysis

• Knowledge of ECO implementation and clock reconstruction (CRPR, useful skew) methodologies

• Experience leading or mentoring a team of physical design engineers on complex SoC projects

• Exposure to memory-centric interfaces and systems such as SSD SoC, HBM, or HBF (High Bandwidth Flash) base die designs (a plus, not required)

• Familiarity with chiplet and die-to-die (D2D) interconnect technologies, including Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) or equivalent D2D PHY protocols (a plus, not required)

COMPENSATION: $160,000/yr - $220,000/yr

REGARDING COMPENSATION:

SK hynix memory solutions America Inc. offers you the opportunity to apply your skills to exciting projects while working with innovative teams. Our compensation package is complimented by a generous benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life insurance and a company 401(k) match, as well as cafeteria, onsite gym and much more. If you are motivated by technical challenges, we offer a collaborative work environment that encourages career growth.

The salary offered to a selected candidate will be tailored based on several factors, including the location, job grade, relevant knowledge, skills, and experience. We also take into account the internal equity among our current team members to ensure fairness and competitiveness.

Duties and Responsibilities

• Responsible for ensuring AZZ’s financial statements are prepared in compliance with U.S. GAAP, including proper assessment of new or changing business activities to ensure ongoing compliance. For complex and/or material activities, obtain guidance from Technical Accounting and implement procedures and controls accordingly.

• Define standardized metrics and telemetry dashboards to deliver actionable risk insights for leadership, enabling proactive tracking of systemic vulnerabilities and cross-team remediation accountability.

jobs.title: Director, Payloads Systems Integration and Test
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About this role

As Director of Payload Systems Integration and Test, you will lead and grow a team of multidisciplinary engineers responsible for end-to-end mission success of a diverse portfolio of payloads, such as inertial, RF, and optical sensors and communication systems, as well as various types of pharmaceutical processing payloads. This role combines deep technical authority with team leadership, product definition, and customer delivery
responsibility. You will own the successful execution of multiple concurrent payload missions, delivering flight hardware that operates in orbit, survives hypersonic reentry, and returns to Earth – reliably and at scale.

Your team will serve as the technical bridge between each payload and the Varda vehicle, defining interfaces, planning and executing payload integration and test campaigns, coordinating in-orbit operations, and ensuring safe recovery of payload data and hardware. When payloads require special accommodations or vehicle modifications, your team will work across the vehicle engineering team to scope and implement these changes.

As Director, you will manage day-to-day execution across the team, in addition to hiring and headcount planning, new project scoping, and development of standard workflows and processes. You will also own and evolve the Varda Payload User Guide, defining standard interfaces and accommodations for hosted payloads, and developing a roadmap that expands the set of customers and use cases Varda can support while simultaneously growing mission cadence.

Responsibilities

• Build and lead the Payload Systems Integration & Test team, hiring and developing engineers across a range of experience levels

jobs.title: Director, Publications & Medical Information
jobs.description:
About Us

Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.

It is Kardigan’s mission to develop multiple targeted treatments in parallel that bring people with cardiovascular diseases to the cures they deserve.

Led by Tassos Gianakakos, Jay Edelberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Bob McDowell, Ph.D., Kardigan’s co-founders have reunited after leading MyoKardia to discover and develop mavacamten, the first cardiac myosin inhibitor, resulting in an acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020.

We have a cutting-edge discovery and translational research platform, a pipeline of late-stage candidates, and an industry-leading team that is driven to improve the lives of patients.

At Kardigan, we are motivated by our values which guide how we work, interact, and achieve our goals. Driven by patients and their families, we are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients and prioritizing their needs above all else. We believe in being authentic—leading with truth to bring out the best in others by creating an environment where every person knows they will be fully accepted. With an eagerness to learn, we encourage the highest levels of curiosity and are open to changing our minds. We are committed to winning as a team with urgency, excellence, and intention, and support each other no matter what role we play or where we sit. Lastly, we strive to enable the impossible because patients are counting on us. We are not afraid to take risks to unlock innovation and advance scientific discoveries.

These values are the foundation of our work, empowering us to make a real difference, every day.

At Kardigan, Medical Affairs serves as the scientific bridge between Research & Development, the external medical community, and future commercial stakeholders. Through evidence generation, scientific communications, and external engagement, we help translate science into meaningful impact for patients and healthcare professionals.

Position Summary

The Director, Publications & Medical Information is a strategic leadership role within Scientific Communications and Medical Affairs responsible for developing and executing integrated evidence dissemination strategies across Kardigan's cardiovascular portfolio.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Scientific Communications, this individual will lead publication strategy, publication governance, scientific narrative execution, medical information operations, and scientific content development to ensure that Kardigan's evidence is communicated effectively, consistently, and compliantly.

The successful candidate will help shape how scientific evidence generated across clinical development, translational research, medical affairs, real-world evidence, and health outcomes research is transformed into impactful publications, congress presentations, medical education, scientific exchange, and medical information resources.

Key Responsibilities

Publications Strategy & Planning

• Co-lead development and execution of integrated publication strategies across all disease areas and development programs.

• Drive alignment between publication plans and broader scientific communication objectives.

• Manage publication agencies and external publication partners.

• Support publication charters and strategic publication plans that align with clinical development milestones, evidence generation strategies, and Medical Affairs objectives.

• Identify publication opportunities across clinical, translational, biomarker, real-world evidence, implementation science, and disease-state education initiatives.

Publication Development & Governance

• Oversee publication development from concept through submission and dissemination.

• Partner with clinical development, biostatistics, regulatory affairs, safety, legal, and research teams throughout publication development.

• Lead publication operations infrastructure including future publication tracking systems, publication dashboards, annual planning processes, publication metrics, budget tracking, and governance workflows.

• Ensure adherence to ICMJE guidelines, GPP standards, authorship policies, Sunshine requirements, and publication-related compliance standards.

• Establish inspection-ready documentation, SOPs, work instructions, and quality management processes supporting publication and medical information activities.

Scientific Narrative & Data Communications

• Partner with Medical Directors and Scientific Communications leadership to develop and maintain scientific narratives and communication platforms across disease states.

• Ensure consistent scientific messaging across publications, congress activities, medical education materials, field medical resources, corporate communications, and investor communications.

Scientific Communications Operations & Excellence

• Lead operational planning, governance, budget management, vendor oversight, and performance reporting across Scientific Communications activities.

• Develop and maintain dashboards and KPIs to measure publication execution, medical information performance, scientific content utilization, and dissemination effectiveness.

• Establish scalable systems, processes, and technologies to support publication management, medical information operations, knowledge management, and launch readiness.

• Identify opportunities to leverage AI and digital solutions to improve efficiency, content development, and insight generation.

Medical Information Leadership

• Build and operationalize Kardigan's Medical Information capabilities as the company advances toward commercialization.

• Lead development and maintenance of:

• Standard Medical Information response documents

• Scientific response letters

• Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

• Medical Information content repositories

• Scientific exchange materials

• Establish and continuously improve inquiry intake, triage, escalation, and response processes.

• Ensure compliance with pharmacovigilance reporting requirements and adverse event identification procedures.

• Analyze inquiry trends and generate insights that inform Medical Strategy, Evidence Generation, and Medical Education priorities.

Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Serve as a strategic thought partner to Medical Affairs leadership.

• Collaborate extensively with Clinical Development, Research, Regulatory Affairs, Field Medical, Patient Advocacy, Commercial Strategy, and External Affairs.

• Contribute to integrated Medical Strategy Planning and evidence dissemination planning.

Qualifications

Required

• PhD, PharmD or equivalent advanced scientific degree.

• Demonstrated leadership in publications strategy and execution.

• Significant experience managing publication agencies and external vendors.

• Strong understanding of publication guidelines, publication ethics, and scientific communications best practices.

• Experience leading cross-functional teams in complex development-stage environments.

• Exceptional scientific writing, communication, and presentation skills.

Preferred

• 10+ years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or medical communications experience preferred

• Cardiovascular disease experience

• Experience supporting launch or pre-launch products

• Medical Information leadership experience

• CMPP certification

Exact Compensation may vary based on skills, experience and location.

Pay range

$200,000—$275,000 USD
